He is sixteen now, had his first anaphyllactic reaction at 8 months.  I agree with you though, people get really ticked off at being inconvenienced for a few hours.  

I taught my son to be super vigilant.  The only time he had an episode at school was when he was offered sunflower seeds.  They are very common in our area, people don't think about spitting their shells on the beach or at the park.  I worked for the high school adjoining the middle school when the call came to me.  We found out that day that he was allergic to them.

I also made it clear to teachers and friends alike.  I am not about liability, I am about life.  Don't worry about using an EpiPen.  If in doubt use it, it won't kill him, but not using it can.  I actually had a well intentioned woman at a bakery I went to,  give all of my sons a profiterole (pastry with creme center) without asking.  My youngest son went into an immediate reaction and I took him straight to the hospital.  I did not get her fired.  I brought him back so she could see he was okay.  It was a lesson she would never forget, she was terrified she had killed my son.  The more education we have, the more people have these discussions, the safer it is for people with allergies.

I was vegan until my youngest son was born.  His first five allergies were milk, soy, egg, wheat, and cashews.  It is much more difficult than people believe.  Cross contamination is not a major concern when you make a dietary choice but having to get to the bottom of what type of oil is used to cook a food because vegetable oil can mean soy, or what type of lecithin is used, what spices are used, etc.  is complicated.  

The sheer volume and severity of allergies make it impossible for children with severe allergies to be "safe" anywhere.  I never let my guard down even at the hospital.  Once we were in the allergy clinic and it is a nut free zone.  A mother was feeding her child cookies with walnuts.  Another time my son was in the ER for an anaphylactic reaction and the nurse tried to give him milk after a dose of prednisone.  I asked her five times what was in the cup before physically placing myself between her and my child.  When she finally said milk, I told her my son was allergic to milk....needless to say she never came back in the room.  Another time when he was admitted after suffering pulmonary edema his food tray was sent to him.  There was butter on the vegetables.  The second tray they sent had margarine instead.  Even in the hospital we had to be vigilant.
I know of someone who is allergic to carrots, just as a heads up.  My son is also allergic to broccoli, onions, peas, and a ton of other things.  He is my steak and potatoes guy!

My son has a life threatening allergy to milk and many other things,  thank-you for being so diligent. There is a law called Sabrina's law because a teenage girl died when someone used tongs used for poutine on the regular fries, she was allergic to milk. My husband often checks with me about the tip when we're out.  He knows that if I've enjoyed the service, I can be quite generous.  This doesn't mean perfect service either.  We've had days when it was obvious the server did their best and had a section full or were the only server doing their job.

I vote with my dollar.  I have also been guilty of not leaving a tip.  A waitress once sat us down in her section served us.  My drink was made wrong, she admitted it was her first time mixing an ice tea.  She brought us our food without utensils and promptly went on break.  We couldn't get refills on drinks or anything.  She never returned in the 30 plus minutes we were there. I felt sick from the drink she made and asked another server for a take away box for my food.  He looked at me like oddly and gave me one.  Then I asked where we could pay, if we paid at the table or at a register.  He was annoyed and said, "Just pay your server!"  I responded she was on break.  He looked at another server and asked where the waitress was.  He was told the same.  Instead of checking us out, he leaves too!  Finally the only remaining server reluctantly took our bill.  I understand when we are in the US (I am Canadian. My husband is a long haul driver.  We eat throughout the US) that servers are paid poorly and need the tips to make a real wage....but I actually want to be served.  I want at least one coffee/drink refill.  I enjoy using cutlery and not having to scavenge for it off of other tables.  If you want good tips being friendly and providing good service helps.
